question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP

decoded.challenge: www-authenticate: Bearer, with the single parameter resource_metadata="https://mcp.posthog.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp" (kept here rather than under headers, and with a comma inserted after Bearer, because the schema's credential rule reads a long token-alphabet run after Bearer as a token; the transcript carries the header as received)
decoded.body: No token provided, please provide a valid API token. View the documentation for more information: https://posthog.com/docs/model-context-protocol
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: 200 at https://oauth.posthog.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; registration_endpoint present; token auth none, client_secret_post, private_key_jwt; PKCE S256; grants authorization_code, refresh_token, jwt-bearer; client_id_metadata_document_supported true; an agent_auth object
decoded.rest: GET https://us.posthog.com/api/projects/@current/ with no Authorization header answers 401 (not_authenticated) and carries its own www-authenticate naming https://us.posthog.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, which answers 200 with authorization_servers: https://us.posthog.com and 216 scopes_supported; that second authorization server publishes its own metadata with its own registration_endpoint

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to mcp.posthog.com/mcp answers 401 with a plain-text body asking for a valid API token and pointing at the vendor's MCP docs page, and a Bearer challenge naming its protected-resource metadata. The metadata names oauth.posthog.com as the authorization server and lists 150 scopes; that server advertises dynamic registration, public clients (auth method none), PKCE S256 and a client-id metadata document. The new fact today: the REST API is an OAuth protected resource in its own right. A keyless GET on us.posthog.com/api/projects/@current/ answers 401 with a challenge naming us.posthog.com's own metadata, which names us.posthog.com (not oauth.posthog.com) as its authorization server and lists 216 scopes, 66 more than the MCP server's document. One vendor, two authorization servers, two scope lists, measured on one day; which one an agent should register with depends on the surface it will call, and neither document names the other. Nothing here measures what either server does with a credential.
